candidate_windows.window_text:
We tested our approach on the datasets PER (Chen et al., 2019) and IBMCS (Bar-Haim et al., 2017), which are the main datasets previously used by our competitors. PER is a set of claims and perspectives constructed from online debate websites while IBMCS is a similar dataset released by IBM. Statistics on both datasets are in Table 1a and 1b. We did not use the datasets proposed in SemEval-2016, Task 6 (Mohammad et al., 2016) and SemEval2017, Task 8 (Derczynski et al., 2017) for the predictions because our work focuses on a binary classification while these datasets also include additional classes such as "neutral", "query", or "comment". Extending our method to predict more than two classes should be seen as future work. We implemented our approach using PyTorch 1.4.0, and a BERT BASE model with 12 layers, 768 hidden size, and 12 attention heads. We finetuned BERT with grid search optimizing the $F_{1}$ on a validation dataset with a learning rates $\{1,2,3,4,5\} \times 10^{-5}$ , batch size $\{24,28,32\}$ , and the Adam optimizer. For our experiments, we used a machine with a TitanX GPU with 12GB RAM. In the following, we first discuss the results using the confidence based $K^{\tau}$ and $\Lambda^{\tau}$ classifiers (Tribridl and Tribridd). Then, we study the performance with our weakly supervised approach. Finally, we provide an analysis on the coverage of the templates for negating the perspectives.
